brief: Plan a group gift for the friend who hosted us at their cabin last weekend.
title: Cabin host thank-you
review: Use the known host and thank-you purpose. Ask about a preference or relevant practical constraint, rather than asking who the recipient is or what the occasion is.

title: Ari’s new baby
review: Recognize the baby context without assuming whether the gift is for the baby, a parent or the family; an open preferences question or that distinction is acceptable.

brief: Plan a group gift for Nina recovering from surgery; she cannot have flowers.
title: Nina recovery gift
review: Do not ask who it is for, why or suggest flowers. Ask about a relevant preference or practical need, and preserve the exclusion.
